ARAB 354.d: Critical examination of Arabic print and digital media with a focus on close reading, critical interpretation, and analysis. Students will work on a variety of media sources, including newspapers, magazines, blogs, academic journals, and news websites that address current political and social topics. From accounts of diplomatic relations and conferences to protests and demonstrations, conflicts and terrorism, and government policy and elections, students will receive practical training in critical reading of news stories in Modern Standard Arabic.
ARAB 354.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

ARAB 264.d: Continuation of ARAB 263. Development of interactional competence in Arabic (sociolinguistic and socio cultural knowledge) to communicate and interact with speakers of Arabic. The course is based on a student-centered, critical-thinking approach to language analysis/acquisition. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for ARAB 264 if student has credit for ARAB 202.
ARAB 264.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

ARAB 334.d: This advanced-level Arabic language and culture course is designed for students who have completed at least four semesters of college-level Arabic or equivalent proficiency. The course constitutes a critical examination of contemporary Arab society and culture through sociocultural, artistic, and media representations, employing a multidisciplinary approach with particular focus on the study abroad location as a case study. Department Permission Required.
ARAB 334.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

ARAB 333.d: This course develops students' interactional competence in Arabic by examining language use as action, context-sensitive communication, and co-constructed meaning making. Designed for students with advanced Arabic proficiency, the course focuses on linguistic and non-linguistic resources that Arabic speakers draw upon to achieve communicative goals in naturalistic settings. Department Permission Required.
ARAB 333.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

ARAB 141.d: This course is for students with no prior knowledge of Arabic. Development of interactional competence in Arabic (sociolinguistic and sociocultural knowledge) to communicate and interact with speakers of Arabic. The course is based on a student-centered, critical-thinking approach to language analysis/acquisition. No prior knowledge of this language is necessary. Effective May 15, 2019, this course does not carry D1 credit. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for ARAB 141 if student has credit for ARAB 161.
ARAB 141.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

ARAB 222.d: This course provides credit for students who have successfully completed approved examinations, such as Advanced Placement and International Baccalaureate exams. This credit counts toward the total credit hours required for graduation. Credit may not be received for both ARAB 222 and ARAB 141. Does not receive distribution credit.
ARAB 222.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.
